api-a close-out: 14 of the 16 items are FIXED and 2 are PARTIAL (R03, R33). Every behavioural fix has a test that fails on the HEAD code and passes after. I proved this by temporarily swapping the HEAD version of each file back in and running the new tests.

The full API e2e suite passes: 19 files, 157 tests, including the Anvil chain suite. API typecheck, unit tests and build, plus @gp/shared and @gp/contracts typecheck/lint/test, all pass. One failure is not mine: `pnpm --filter @gp/api lint` reports 680 errors, all inside apps/api/.dist-kit/**. That is another agent's build output, and eslint does not ignore it. `eslint src test prisma scripts` is clean.

Nothing is committed. No web files were changed, so I did not run the web build; the web unit tests pass against the updated @gp/shared. No .next-co-api-a was created, .dev/dist-co-api-a was created for the build check and removed, and no anvil processes remain.

What changed, by area:

- **Chain**
  - `BlockchainService.verifiedClient()` checks eth_chainId once per process and fails closed on a mismatch. The signer, the deposit watcher and the VRF provider all use it (R31).
  - `ChainSignerService.track()` now marks a transaction `dropped` only when two things hold: its nonce was consumed at least `confirmations` blocks deep (checked at head−N+1), and a second receipt lookup made after that nonce read still finds nothing (R01).

- **Withdrawals**
  - A per-player `pg_advisory_xact_lock` is taken before today's usage is read, so concurrent requests cannot together exceed the daily limit (R02).
  - The second approval claims the first one with `updateMany({id, status:'pending'})` and returns CONFLICT unless exactly one row changed (R22).
  - First approvals now carry `payload.expiresAt` (FOUR_EYES_EXPIRY_HOURS). A second approval on an expired one marks it expired, writes a system audit row and starts a new first approval (R23).
  - The broadcaster reads the hot wallet's balance and nonce at one block. Under the signer's nonce row lock it subtracts the transfers already signed but not mined. If that leaves too little, nothing is stored or sent and the withdrawal stays queued (R56).

- **Deposits**
  - Logs are grouped per transaction and per (recipient, amount). Every distinct (txHash, logIndex) becomes its own deposit (R14).
  - A reversed deposit whose transfer comes back reopens the same row. It posts `deposit_detected` again under a versioned event key; reversals are versioned the same way (R15).
  - All deposits of one transaction are re-indexed together inside one DB transaction, through temporary negative indices. Errors are contained to the transaction concerned, so one bad row no longer stops the watcher (R35).
  - Before crediting, `DepositsService.creditHold()` checks account_suspended / deposits_blocked, a break or self-exclusion, the deposits.enabled flag, and RG deposit limits. A held deposit stays in Pending (not stakeable), the player is notified once, and it is re-checked on every pass (R03).

- **Rounds and randomness**
  - Mirroring is decided per round: a `chain_mirror` round is refused with an ALERT if the mirror is off or the provider is not Chainlink. Settlement verifies the draw against the contract inside `settle()` (R21).
  - New env rule: RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink requires POOL_ONCHAIN_MIRROR=true. A round that was never mirrored while Chainlink is active is cancelled with refunds VRF_TIMEOUT_HOURS after its close. A persistent RandomnessNotReadyError is logged as an ALERT every 10 ticks (R10).
  - The VRF provider reads the request id and the VRF word from `getRound()` at a block that already has the required confirmations. Events are used only for tx hashes, best effort (R24).
  - Entry history scopes refunds and wins to each purchase by `entry.transactionId` (R16).
  - Odds are rounded down (ROUND_DOWN), and the API returns them with 6 decimals (R48).

- **Contract (R33)**
  - `requestDraw` is allowed only from Committed, so randomness is never re-requested.
  - New `REASON_VRF_TIMEOUT = 5`: `cancelRound` from DrawRequested is permissionless once DRAW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT has passed. A late fulfilment is ignored.
  - `DrawRequestPending` is replaced by `DrawNotTimedOut`.
  - Forge tests and invariants are updated; the ABI, artifacts and gas snapshot are regenerated.
  - The API keeper calls `cancelForVrfTimeout` and then refunds in the DB.
  - CONTRACTS.md, the contracts README, API.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and the .env.example comment are updated.
  - The existing GP-13 web copy ("No random word arrived within 24 h…") already matches, so I did not touch web.

Edits outside my owned paths, all small and additive:
- `apps/api/src/config/env.ts` and `env.spec.ts`: the R10 rule and its test. api-b is editing these files in parallel; my change is one block.
- `apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts`: added the 'deposit.held' type.
- `packages/shared/src/demo/rounds.ts`: the DEMO odds example now uses the computed, rounded-down 0.187.
- `.env.example`: one comment.
- Docs: API.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CONTRACTS.md, packages/contracts/README.md.

Other side effects:
- `pnpm --filter @gp/api build` rewrote apps/api/dist (the standard nest output). I also built into .dev/dist-co-api-a and then removed it.
- While proving the deposit tests fail on HEAD, the old watcher left two open fake-chain deposits in globalpool_test. I reversed them with balanced postings, and no open non-DEMO deposits remain. The new deposit test cleans up after itself in afterAll.

items.test: unit src/modules/blockchain/chain-signer.spec.ts (4 tests; 3 fail on HEAD: a just-mined transfer was marked dropped)
items.note: A tx is only marked dropped when its nonce was used at least `confirmations` blocks deep (getTransactionCount at head-N+1) and a second receipt lookup made after that read still finds nothing. Otherwise it stays pending. Receipt handling was extracted into fromReceipt().

items.test: e2e withdrawals-closeout: 3 concurrent 900.00 requests against a 2,000 level_1 limit -> exactly 2 succeed (all 3 succeed on HEAD)
items.note: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('withdrawal-limit:'||userId)) is taken at the top of the idempotent transaction, before today's usage is read.

items.test: e2e deposit-watcher (R03 cases: deposits_blocked held then credited after lift; self-excluded held; weekly 500 limit -> 300 credited, 300 held). All fail on HEAD.
items.note: Implemented as a hold: the confirmed deposit stays in PENDING (not stakeable, tx status under_review 'On hold — …'), the player gets a one-time deposit.held notice, and an ALERT is logged. It is re-checked every pass and credited automatically once the block clears. Checks run against account_suspended/deposits_blocked, an active break or self-exclusion, the deposits.enabled flag, and RG deposit limits counted on deposits credited in the current period. Owner decisions still needed: (1) the suggested withdraw-only bucket does not exist. OWED is claimable to Available, so I did not use it, and held funds cannot be withdrawn by the player while held; how they are returned is an owner/ops decision. (2) A deposit that would exceed a limit is held as a whole, not only the excess. (3) Geo is not evaluated, because a chain deposit has no request location.

items.test: unit env.spec 'refuses RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink without the on-chain mirror'; e2e rounds-closeout R10 (fails on HEAD: round stayed closed forever)
items.note: The reverse cross-field rule is added. In startDraw, a round that is not mirrored while the Chainlink provider is active raises RandomnessNotReadyError and an ALERT, and is cancelled with refunds (reason vrf_timeout) VRF_TIMEOUT_HOURS after its close. The tick logs an ALERT for a persistent RandomnessNotReadyError every 10 ticks.

items.test: e2e deposit-watcher R14: two identical 100.00 Transfers in one tx -> 2 deposits, 200.00 credited (HEAD detects 1)
items.note: Scanned logs are grouped by tx and (to, amount). A log is skipped as a moved copy only when a live deposit of the same transfer lost its own index; every other distinct (txHash, logIndex) is recorded.

items.test: e2e deposit-watcher R15: detected -> re-orged -> reversed -> re-included -> reopened -> credited once; postings detected, reversed, detected, credited (HEAD never credits)
items.note: Rejected rows are excluded from the moved-copy check. The same row is reopened: status confirming, deposit_detected posted again under the key deposit:<id>:detected:<n>, and reversals versioned as deposit:<id>:reversed:<n>. One transfer is always one deposit.

items.test: e2e pool-history R16 (2 tests: 35+10 entries in a cancelled round -> 350.00 and 100.00; a win shows only on the purchase whose entry won). Both fail on HEAD.
items.note: Winners and refund counts are scoped by entry.transactionId. Entries without a purchase link fall back to the round.

items.test: e2e rounds-closeout R21 (2 tests: no mock draw for a chain_mirror round; no DB vrf_timeout refund or off-chain settle). Both fail on HEAD.
items.note: mirrored() is now per round: if chain_mirror is set and the mirror is disabled or the provider is not Chainlink, it throws MirrorUnavailableError and logs an ALERT, so nothing is drawn, cancelled or settled off-chain. settle() verifies the draw against the contract for chain_mirror rounds. sync() and pendingRounds() also re-mirror vrf_timeout cancellations.

items.test: e2e withdrawals-closeout 'a second approval racing the requester withdrawing…' (the interleaving is injected deterministically; on HEAD the withdrawal is queued)
items.note: The approval is claimed with updateMany({id, status:'pending'}) and a CONFLICT is returned unless count === 1.

items.test: e2e withdrawals-closeout: first approval has expiresAt ≈ +4 h; a stale approval -> expired + approval.expired system audit row + a new first approval, withdrawal stays under_review (fails on HEAD)
items.note: Rows without an expiresAt fall back to createdAt + FOUR_EYES_EXPIRY_HOURS. FourEyesService.expireStale now expires these rows too, because it reads payload.expiresAt.

items.test: chain e2e (Anvil) R24: with the event window placed past the events, the request id and word still come from getRound and the round settles (on HEAD it stays waiting)
items.note: fulfillment() reads getRound at head - confirmations + 1. request() falls back to getRound.lastRequestId. getLogs is best effort and only supplies tx hashes.

items.test: unit blockchain.spec (refuses chain 42161, mismatch never cached, watcher skips without getLogs or recordDetected)
items.note: The check fails closed with ChainUnavailableError and an ALERT log. The watcher and the VRF provider now use the verified client.

items.test: forge: test_RequestDraw_NeverReRequested, test_VrfTimeout_AnyoneCancelsOnlyAfterTimeout, test_VrfTimeout_LateFulfilmentIsIgnored, test_VrfTimeout_FulfilmentBeforeCancelIsFinal, plus the updated invariant (drawAttempts ≤ 1, a requested draw is only cancelled for VRF_TIMEOUT). Chain e2e R33: 25 h without fulfilment -> on-chain cancel with reason 5 -> DB refund -> late fulfilment ignored.
items.note: Not proven fail-before. I did not swap the old contract back in, so no test was run against the pre-fix code; this is why it is PARTIAL rather than FIXED. The new forge and chain tests check behaviour the old contract did not have (it allowed a re-request after 24 h and reverted a cancel from DrawRequested). The change itself follows the owner policy: there is no re-request; a permissionless cancelRound(REASON_VRF_TIMEOUT = 5) is allowed only from DrawRequested after DRAW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, and the API keeper calls it before the DB refund. The GP-13 web copy already describes a cancel and refund after 24 h, so web is unchanged. The contract is still unaudited and not deployed.

items.test: e2e deposit-watcher R35: X@7, Y@8 re-included at X@8, Y@9 -> pass ok, both re-indexed and credited (HEAD: 'skipped: reconcile failed')
items.note: reindex() gives each open deposit of a tx a distinct matching log. Moves go through temporary negative indices in one DB transaction, reversed rows holding a needed index are parked, and credited or out-of-scope rows keep their slots. Errors are contained per transaction.

items.test: shared unit 'odds are rounded down, never up (R48)' (2/3 -> 66.666, 1/1500 -> 0.066); e2e my-entries odds 2/3 -> '66.666666' (66.666667 before)
items.note: pct() uses ROUND_DOWN. The API my-entries odds use 6 decimals. The DEMO odds example now uses the computed value (0.187 instead of the hardcoded 0.188).

items.test: chain e2e (Anvil) R56: hot wallet 100, two concurrent 60.00 broadcasts -> ['broadcast','queued'] (HEAD: ['broadcast','broadcast'] -> on-chain revert)
items.note: Balance and nonce are read at one block. Under the signer's nonce row lock (in onStored), the net amounts of in-flight withdrawal txs with nonce ≥ that block's nonce are subtracted; if too little remains it throws HotWalletShortError, stores and sends nothing, and the withdrawal stays queued. The secondary suggestion is not implemented: an on-chain ERC20InsufficientBalance revert still fails the withdrawal and refunds it. Re-queuing would need a new broadcast→queued transition and revert-reason decoding.

decisions: R03 needs an owner decision: on-chain deposits that hit a restriction, self-exclusion, the kill switch or an RG deposit limit are held in PENDING (never stakeable) and credited automatically once the block clears. The suggested 'withdraw-only bucket' was not built: OWED is claimable to Available, so it would bypass the limit, and a new held bucket plus a withdraw-from-held path would mean a schema, wallet and UI change. Held funds therefore cannot be withdrawn by the player while held, and the owner/ops must define how they are returned. A deposit that would exceed a limit is held as a whole, not split. Geo is not evaluated for chain deposits.

R03 gate: deposit limits are counted on deposits CREDITED in the current period (creditedAt), not RG's createdAt-based usage. This keeps holds in credit order, and a deposit held over into a new period counts in that period. Due pending increases or removals are read as effective, without being persisted.

R10: a round that was never mirrored while the Chainlink provider is active is cancelled with reason 'vrf_timeout' (stakes to Owed, fees not refunded) VRF_TIMEOUT_HOURS after its close, rather than immediately. I reused the existing reason so the web copy and enums need no change.

R33: VRF-timeout cancellation is permissionless (same model as the THRESHOLDS_NOT_MET cancel), reason code 5. DrawRequestPending was replaced by DrawNotTimedOut, a breaking ABI change; the contract is not deployed. drawAttempts is kept in the struct (always ≤ 1) for ABI stability.
R33: the GP-13 web copy already says 'No random word arrived within 24 h of the request…', so web was not changed (web pool components are outside my paths).

R56: the race is fixed at the root by reserving in-flight transfers under the signer's nonce row lock. Re-queuing after an on-chain ERC20InsufficientBalance revert was not implemented: it would need a broadcast→queued transition and decoding the revert of a mined tx. The withdrawal still fails with a full refund, so nothing is lost.
R23: withdrawal first approvals use the same FOUR_EYES_EXPIRY_HOURS (4 h) as the other four-eyes requests, as suggested. An expired one is replaced by a new first approval from the admin who acted.

Edits outside my owned paths: config/env.ts + env.spec.ts (R10 rule; api-b is editing these too, my change is one block), notifications.service.ts ('deposit.held' union member), packages/shared/src/demo/rounds.ts (DEMO odds example now computed and rounded down), .env.example (one comment), docs (API.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CONTRACTS.md, contracts README). deposits.controller.ts was modified by another agent (R27), not by me.

Memory: the stored notes are about Figma files and were not relevant, so none were used. Learned this session and possibly worth saving: apps/api `pnpm lint` picks up other agents' `.dist-*` build directories (no eslint ignore), and the API test DB is shared, so watcher e2e tests must reverse their own open on-chain deposits (other watcher suites reconcile every open row).

report:
All 20 api-b items are done: 19 FIXED and R55 PARTIAL (entry purchases now count as play time; the games engine does not yet record activity on DEMO bets). Each behavioural fix has a test that fails on the old code and passes now, except R52 and R60, which are config-only and were checked by command.

**Before/after proof.** I swapped the HEAD versions of my files in temporarily, ran the tests, then restored them (diff confirmed):

items.test: src/config/env.spec.ts 'placeholder secrets (R04)' (3 unit tests) + test/security-closeout.e2e-spec.ts 'R04 … never carries the raw session family id'
items.note: With NODE_ENV=production, boot is refused when JWT_*, ADMIN_JWT_*, TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY or ENTRY_SALT_ENCRYPTION_KEY equals an .env.example value or contains dev-only / change-me / placeholder (checked raw and base64-decoded). decisions: R06 scope: 6m / 1y / 5y self-exclusions never reopen automatically (request, then 24 h cool-down, then a deposit limit and a loss limit, then explicit confirm). Cooling-off breaks (24 h / 7 d / 30 d) still end on their date, as the RG6 screens promise ('limits stay exactly as they are') and as in common time-out practice. Permanent cannot be reopened in-app. Reopen is player self-serve from the RG7 page, not via support, and the restricted-page copy now says 'Ask to reopen'. If the owner wants support to approve reopening, that needs an admin workflow and is a business decision.
R06 migration grandfathers self-exclusions that had already ended (reopened_at = ends_at), so DEMO accounts are not closed again retroactively.
R06 'limits reviewed' means a deposit limit and a loss limit must exist when the player confirms; an explicit confirm step is required even if both were set earlier.

R28: backup codes are accepted, but a long self-exclusion with no 2FA proof at all was not enabled (it needs an owner decision because of griefing risk with a stolen session). A locked step-up points the player to an immediate cooling-off break instead.

R04: no separate STEP_UP_SECRET, because JWT_ACCESS_SECRET is used only for step-up tokens and is now covered by the production placeholder guard. PRIVY_MOCK_SIGNING_SECRET is not checked in production because the DEV MOCK is refused there.
R50: chose a uniform lockout per email hash (Redis) for unknown emails rather than a generic 401 for locked accounts, which keeps the designed ADM-01 locked state in the web.

R55: Global Pool entry purchases count as activity using the same applyHeartbeat logic, including its 120 s credit cap per gap. Game bets are not wired because that is the games agent's path; rg.recordActivity is exported for them.

R19: any authenticated admin request counts as activity (throttled to one write per minute) and a refresh starts a fresh row; the server idle limit is a backstop for closed or discarded tabs, while the client-side 15-minute timer still handles an open idle tab.

R44: the breaker e2e now always repairs the shared kill switch and expires pending breaker requests before it starts. On the shared test DB this could also expire a breaker request that another agent's concurrent run has open at that moment (a window of about 2 s).

Rules:

- Commas in complete groups of three digits are thousands separators and are stripped.
- Any other lone ',' is a decimal point.
